newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank boss says foreign debt falling.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank boss says foreign debt falling.

text.p: Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanonda said that he was satisfied with the country's short-term debt level which was declining.
Rerngchai said the outstanding foreign debt at the end of November stood at US$88.9 billion, $39.6 billion or 44.6 percent of which was short-term debt.
The BOT governor said the trend is more satisfactory compared with that in 1995 when the short-term debt accounted for 49.8 percent of the total foreign debt.
"The Bank of Thailand is satisfied with the current level of foreign debt. The adjustment between the proportion of short-term debt and long-term is seen as a good trend," he said.
He attributed the decline in the short-term debt level on the Bank of Thailand's slew of measures to curb short-term borrowing.

High level short-term debt has raised concerns among economists and investors who said such debt put Thailand in a vulnerable postion given its huge current account deficit which was projected to reach 8.2 percent of GDP in 1996.
